newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ASTLE, MORRISON STAGE GREAT ESCAPE FOR NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ASTLE, MORRISON STAGE GREAT ESCAPE FOR NZ.

text.p: All-rounder Nathan Astle hit his third test century and veteran bowler Danny Morrison proved an unlikely batting hero as New Zealand defied England to snatch a draw in the first cricket test on Tuesday.
The last wicket pair staged one of New Zealand's greatest escapes in test matches, tormenting the English attack for 165 minutes with an unbroken partnership of 106.

England, desperate for a test victory after their disastrous tour of Zimbabwe, looked certain winners when they reduced New Zealand to 105 for eight at lunch, still needing 26 to make the tourists bat again.
Simon Doull gave Astle initial support with an aggressive 26 before being yorked by Darren Gough.
Then Morrison, holder of the world record for the highest number of ducks in tests, defended stoutly with a match-saving innings of 14 not out from 133 balls.
Morrison, describing himself as "a bit of an underachiever" with the bat, told reporters: "I had nothing to lose and everything to gain. I just wanted to play on for Nathan."
Astle said his third test century, and his first on New Zealand soil, was the most satisfying to date. Punishing anything loose, he struck 13 fours and batted for 279 minutes, facing 214 balls.
England captain Mike Atherton flung all five bowlers into the attack by turn, but failed to achieve a breakthrough.

"It proved difficult to dislodge them because the wicket was so dead," Atherton said. "We'll go into the next test match knowing that we've got what it takes. I'm slightly disappointed not to have won, but life goes on."
Morrison and Astle added an unbroken 106 for the last wicket, smashing the previous record of 57 for New Zealand's 10th wicket against England, set by Frank Mooney and Jack Cowie at Leeds in 1949.
It was the third stand of more than 100 for the 10th wicket by New Zealand in test cricket.
Earlier, fine spin bowling by left-armer Phil Tufnell, backed by seamer Alan Mullally and assisted by some rash batting shots, had put England in a commanding position.
New Zealand, resuming at 56 for three, began confidently but soon lost captain Lee Germon, run out by a direct throw by Nasser Hussain.
Justin Vaughan was then trapped lbw by Tufnell from a ball which spun viciously from the rough.
Adam Parore danced down the wicket to Tufnell and was easily stumped by Stewart for 33.
Mullally then chipped in by inducing Chris Cairns to chop a ball on to his stumps and had Dipak Patel leg before for nought last ball before lunch.
Tufnell finished with three for 53 from 40 overs, while Mullally claimed two for 47 and Darren Gough took two for 66.
The second test starts in Wellington on February 6, before which England play a four-day match against New Zealand A beginning in Wanganui on Thursday.
